import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { resetAndSeed } from '../support/seed';

// Part of an invoice can be written off as bad debt. The written-off part stops counting as owed;
// the rest still does.
test.describe('partial write-off', () => {
  test('writes off part of an invoice', { tag: '@functionality' }, async ({ page }) => {
    await resetAndSeed({
      clients: [{ id: 1, name: 'Acme Ltd', email: 'ops@acme.example' }],
      projects: [{ id: 1, name: 'Website Rebuild', clientId: 1 }],
      invoices: [{ id: 1, projectId: 1, status: 'SENT', writeOff: 40, lineItems: [{ id: 1, description: 'Work', qty: 1, unitPrice: 100 }] }],
    });
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByTestId('nav-projects').click();
    await page.getByTestId('project-open-1').click();
    await page.getByTestId('invoice-open-1').click();

    await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-write-off-amount')).toHaveText('$40.00');
    await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-due-amount')).toHaveText('$60.00');
  });
});

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build, start the whole app, run the Playwright specs present in e2e/specs, then stop.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL.
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the Spring Boot app on $PORT (main class net.officefloor.hq.app.Application). On boot, Flyway
# migrates the empty in-memory H2 up to the current schema; Spring serves the SPA (static/) and the
# app's REST endpoints; the `e2e` profile enables the /__test__ seed endpoint. Returns once
# launching; poll /actuator/health for readiness.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
mkdir -p .run

: "${PORT:?PORT must be set}"
JAR="$(ls -t target/*.jar 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
[ -n "$JAR" ] || { echo "no jar in target/ — run bin/build first" >&2; exit 1; }

# Known audit file (the file-based test-assertion channel). Absolute so app + tests agree.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

nohup java -jar "$JAR" --server.port="$PORT" --spring.profiles.active=e2e > .run/app.log 2>&1 &
echo $! > .run/app.pid
/tmp/start.log
e2e
target

content.text:
You can now write off part of an invoice as bad debt. The acceptance test passes with `bin/e2e`: an invoice for $100.00 with $40.00 written off shows **$40.00 written off** and **$60.00 owed**.

I also called the new endpoint directly against the running app. Writing off $40.00 of a $100.00 invoice left $60.00 owed. Asking to write off $70.00 next was rejected (HTTP 422). Writing off the last $60.00 turned it into a full write-off with nothing owed. Both steps were written to the audit log.

**What changed**
- **Database:** a new migration, `V81__invoice_partial_write_off.sql`, adds a written-off amount to each invoice. It defaults to 0 and can't be negative.
- **Server:**
  - The invoice keeps a running total of what has been written off, and that amount no longer counts as owed.
  - Something written off counts as part-settled, so the invoice reads PARTIAL. If payments, credits and write-offs together cover the whole amount, it reads PAID.
  - The new endpoint is `POST /api/projects/{p}/invoices/{i}/write-off-part` with `{amount}`. It only works on sent or part-paid invoices, and the amount must be above zero and no more than what's still owed. Writing off exactly what's left does the existing full write-off instead.
  - A partial write-off is audited as `INVOICE_PART_WRITTEN_OFF id=… amount=…`.
  - The invoice detail now includes the written-off amount, and the test seed accepts a `writeOff` value.
- **Front end:**
  - On the invoice page, a sent or part-paid invoice now has a "Write off part" form next to the existing full write-off button. It checks the amount and shows an error if the server rejects it.
  - When something has been written off, a "Written off as bad debt" row (`invoice-write-off-amount`) appears just above the amount owed. No existing `data-testid` was renamed or removed.

**Two things to know**
- **Dashboard totals:** some outstanding totals on the dashboard are added up straight from invoice amounts in the database, so they still ignore partial write-offs. The invoice page, client statements and the dashboard figures worked out invoice by invoice do reflect them. Updating the rest is a follow-up if you want it.
- **The server is Spring Boot, not OfficeFloor:** your request mentioned an OfficeFloor server, but the app is a standard Spring Boot application (the `net.officefloor.hq` name is just the package). I followed its existing Spring conventions.
